# DubStemMix

> Free, open-source (MIT) dub mixing console for macOS, built for the Akai MIDImix. Put the stems of a tune on six faders, play the effects on the last two, and cut your own dub live, the way it was done at King Tubby's: pull the vocal, throw the snare into the echo, drop everything but bass and drums, let the spring crash. No DAW, no session to prepare, nothing to map.

Made by YoanDev (https://yoandev.co). Source, releases and issues: https://github.com/yoanbernabeu/DubStemMix

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 15 or later, Apple Silicon only (built and tested on macOS 26). Not tested on Intel.
- Price: free. License: MIT. Signed ad hoc, not notarized (Open Anyway once, or use the install script).
- Controller: Akai MIDImix on its factory mapping. Optional: everything also works with mouse and keyboard. Other controllers with the same geometry can be added as a data profile (`ControllerProfile`).
- Install, one line: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yoanbernabeu/DubStemMix/main/install.sh | sh` (installs or updates DubStemMix.app in /Applications, clears the Gatekeeper quarantine flag, opens the app). Or download the zip from the releases page.
- Input: any audio stems (WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, M4A, CAF), any sample rate. Several stems can share a strip.
- Stem separation built in: drop a full song, get drums, bass, instruments and vocals on strips 1 to 4 (htdemucs_ft through ONNX Runtime, on the CPU, about 1.2x the song length on an M3 Pro, up to 9 GB of memory). The 663 MB model is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use, after asking, never bundled.
- Output: 24-bit WAV recording of the master (after the limiter). Projects (.dubstem) and setlists (.dubset), built in a setlist workshop (library with search, a colour and a tag per line, listening before adding).

## The board

Eight strips mirrored on screen: 1 to 6 hold the stems, 7 and 8 play the effects. Per strip: three knobs, MUTE, REC ARM, a fader. BANK LEFT / BANK RIGHT switch what the knobs do; stem faders stay strip volumes.

- MIX page: knobs are sends to DELAY, REVERB, BUS 3.
- FX page: knobs drive the built-in effects (delay time, feedback, wow, filters, reverb decay, damping, tone, phaser rate, depth) and the three returns.
- MASTER page: the big knob, the kills, the dubplate colour, delay heads and ping-pong.
- INSERTS page: each strip's insert (sub-octave, auto-wah, or a plugin's macros).
- MUTE cuts a strip; SOLO held + MUTE solos in place. REC ARM held is the dub throw: the strip goes at full level into the delay and/or reverb, pre-fader and pre-mute.
- Effect strips 7 and 8 (MIX page): knobs are delay speed, delay feedback, reverb length, phaser rate and the delay / reverb bus-to-bus sends; faders are the delay and reverb returns on every page; buttons held are HOLD, x2 (delay twice as fast), FX ONLY (dry sound out, effects still fed) and TAPE STOP (the delay's tape brakes to a standstill).
- Effects sit on shared buses: cutting a strip never kills an echo or reverb tail already on its way. Sends are post-fader by default, switchable to pre-fader per bus.

## Gestures (keyboard or master column buttons)

D (hold) drop: everything cut but the strips marked KEEP. H (hold) hold: the delay closes on itself, feedback at unity. C crash: hit the spring reverb. R pull-up: tape brake on the master, back to the top, play. T tap tempo. N / P next and previous tune of the setlist. Esc panic: empties the delay, reverb and bus 3. Cmd+R record the master.

## The sound (all built in, no plugin needed)

- Dub delay: tape echo, every pass through filters and saturation, feedback up to self-oscillation, wow and flutter, time in ms or tempo-locked (1/16 to 1/2, dotted), Space Echo head patterns (1, 2, 3, 1+2, 2+3, 1+3, 1+2+3), ping-pong.
- Reverb: Dattorro plate, or a dispersive spring (with the CRASH gesture).
- Bus 3: Bi-Phase-style phaser (two six-stage phasers in series) or a tape flanger; both output only the shifted signal.
- Master chain: King Tubby's stepped high-pass (20 Hz to 10 kHz in twelve steps), sound-system isolator kills (BASS / MID / TOP, kill only), dubplate colour (bandwidth loss, tape saturation, wobble, crackle), pull-up.
- Strip inserts: sub-octave generator (dbx boom box idea), Mu-Tron III style auto-wah.
- Any Audio Unit effect can replace a built-in effect on a bus or sit in an insert; plugins load out of process, a crash falls back to the built-in effect.

## Known limits

Plugin latency is not compensated. Loading or removing a plugin, or putting a stem on a strip, is refused while playing (it would cut the sound); switching plate/spring or phaser/flanger is gapless. MUTE takes about 25 ms to close. Only the MIDImix is supported in this version.
